questions.q: Who is recognized as the first registered architect in the Philippines?
questions.n: He holds the distinction of being the first registered architect in the Philippines, holding license number 001.

questions.q: In what year was the first architect's license in the Philippines issued to Tomas Mapua?
questions.n: The first architectural license was issued in 1921 following the passage of Act No. 2985, which regulated the practice of the profession.

questions.q: Tomas Mapua was part of a group of Filipino students sent to study in the United States. What was this program called?
questions.n: This government-funded program sent talented Filipino students to the US for higher education to prepare them for leadership roles in the Philippines.

questions.q: At which American university did Tomas Mapua earn his degree in Architecture?
questions.n: Mapua graduated from Cornell University in 1911 before returning to the Philippines to practice.

questions.q: Which of these government agencies did Tomas Mapua work for as a supervising architect?
questions.n: Mapua served in this bureau, where he contributed to the design of many early 20th-century public buildings.

questions.q: What educational institution did Tomas Mapua found in 1925?
questions.n: He founded this school to provide high-quality technical education to Filipinos, particularly in engineering and architecture.

questions.q: The St. La Salle Hall at De La Salle University, known for its neoclassical style, was designed by which architect?
questions.n: He was the architect of this iconic H-shaped building, which is a prime example of neoclassical architecture in Manila.

questions.q: Which prominent hospital in Manila features a design by Tomas Mapua?
questions.n: Mapua was involved in the architectural design of this hospital located in Tondo, Manila.

questions.q: Tomas Mapua's architectural style is often associated with which movement that was popular during the American colonial period?
questions.n: His works, such as the St. La Salle Hall, reflect the neoclassical aesthetic favored by American planners for public and institutional buildings.

questions.q: Beyond his architectural practice, Mapua was significant for promoting which of the following?
questions.n: By being the first licensed architect and founding a technical institute, he standardized the path for future Filipino architects and engineers.

questions.q: Which specific law, passed in 1921, created the Board of Examiners for Architecture and allowed for the registration of Tomas Mapúa?
questions.n: This landmark legislation formally regulated the practice of architecture, engineering, and surveying in the Philippines.

questions.q: True or False: Tomas Mapúa was the first Filipino to ever graduate from an American architectural school.
questions.n: He was among the first wave of Pensionados and returned with a degree from Cornell in 1911.

questions.q: Before founding his own institute, Tomas Mapúa worked for the government. What was his primary role at the Bureau of Public Works?
questions.n: In this capacity, he oversaw the design and construction of various provincial and municipal buildings.

questions.q: The Mapúa Institute of Technology was originally located in which historic district of Manila?
questions.n: The school was first established in a rented building in this bustling district before moving to Intramuros.

questions.q: What was the original name of the school founded by Tomas Mapúa in 1925?
questions.n: This name has been used since its inception to emphasize its focus on technical and vocational skills.

questions.q: Which building material did Tomas Mapúa frequently specify for the large-scale public buildings he designed in the Neoclassical style?
questions.n: This was the primary structural material introduced by Americans for fire-resistant, monumental public works.

questions.q: In the context of the St. La Salle Hall, which architectural element is a hallmark of the Neoclassical style used by Mapúa?
questions.n: The use of classical orders like Corinthian or Ionic columns is a key feature of Neoclassical facades.

questions.q: Tomas Mapúa served as a city councilor for which city, showing his involvement in civic life?
questions.n: He was elected to the Manila Municipal Board, contributing his expertise to the city's development.

questions.q: What is the primary reason the 'Pensionado Program' was significant for the development of Philippine architecture?
o: It was established by the Spanish government.
It prohibited the use of local materials.
It focused solely on landscape architecture.
It introduced Western formal education and licensing standards.
questions.n: By sending students to the US, the program brought back modern professional standards and technical training.

questions.q: Which of these is a lasting legacy of Tomas Mapúa in the 21st century?
o: The design of the CCP Complex.
The continuous operation of the Mapúa University.
The creation of the first earthquake-proof skyscraper.
The invention of the Bahay Kubo.
questions.n: The school he founded remains one of the premier institutions for architecture and engineering in the country.

questions.q: Tomas Mapúa holds a unique place in history as the holder of the very first license for architects. What is his license number?
questions.n: As the first to be registered under the 1921 law, he was assigned the first sequential number in the registry.

questions.q: Which major body of water was the Mapúa Institute of Technology originally located near in the Quiapo district?
questions.n: The school's original location in Quiapo placed it near this vital waterway that flows through the heart of Manila.

questions.q: What is the primary reason why architects during the time of Tomas Mapúa were required to be licensed?
o: To ensure public safety and professional standards
To increase the cost of building houses
To limit the number of buildings in Manila
To prevent people from using wood
questions.n: Licensing was introduced to regulate the profession so that only qualified individuals could design safe buildings.

questions.q: True or False: Tomas Mapúa returned to the Philippines immediately after finishing his high school education in the United States.
questions.n: He stayed to complete his university degree in Architecture at Cornell before returning to practice.

questions.q: The architectural style 'Neoclassicism' used by Mapúa often features high ceilings and large windows. What was a practical benefit of this in the Philippines?
o: Making the building easier to paint
Keeping the building warm during winter
questions.n: In a tropical climate, high ceilings and large openings help heat rise and air circulate, cooling the interior.

questions.q: Which of these is a common feature of the 'Pensionado' architects' education in America?
o: Focus on modern engineering and sanitation
Learning how to build traditional nipa huts
questions.n: The American curriculum emphasized up-to-date structural methods and health standards for urban buildings.

questions.q: In the early 1900s, who was the primary employer for many Filipino architects like Mapúa who had just returned from studies abroad?
questions.n: Most early architects worked for the Bureau of Public Works to help build the country's infrastructure.

questions.q: Which of these words best describes the appearance of a 'Neoclassical' building designed by Tomas Mapúa?
questions.n: Neoclassical architecture relies heavily on balance and symmetry in its facades and floor plans.

questions.q: True or False: The licensing of architects in the Philippines was a way to recognize architecture as a distinct profession from civil engineering.
questions.n: The 1921 law helped define the specific roles and expertise required for architects as separate from engineers.

questions.q: What title is often given to Tomas Mapúa due to his role in founding the Mapúa Institute of Technology?
questions.n: Beyond his buildings, his work in founding and leading a technical school makes him a key figure in Philippine education.
